test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 18th November 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Mukul lent ₹9,300 on simple interest in two parts. He earned 5% per annum on the first part and 8% per annum on the second part. The total interest he received after 4 years is ₹2,400. What is the ratio of the money lent at 5% to that lent at 8%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Let total amount give on 5%, then SI for 1 year = 9300 x 5 x 1 /100 = 465

Again Let total amount give on 8%, then SI for 1 year = 9300 x 8 x 1/100 = 744

Total interest in 4 year = 2400

Interest for 1 year = 2400/4 = 600

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/49c57946dbf842b1430c1646fa1a90ff04bcfe2dd555d9401b7ff99ccdd2c8e4.png] 

Required Ratio = 144 : 135 = 16 : 15

**∴ Required Ratio = 16 : 15.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Given:

Total principle = Rs. 9300

Interest at 4 years = Rs. 2400

**Formula used:**

Simple interest = (Principle x Rate per annum x Time)/100

**Calculation:**

Let money lent on 5% = a

⇒ Then money lent on 8% = 9300 - a

Interest on 4 year = 2400

⇒ then interest on 1 year = 2400/4

⇒ Rs. 600

According to question,

(a times 5 times 1)/(100) + ((9300 - a) times 8 times 1)/(100) = 600

⇒ (5a)/(100) + (74400 - 8a)/(100) = 600

⇒ (-3a + 74400)/(100) = 600

⇒ - 3a + 74400 = 60000

⇒ 3a = 14400

⇒ a = 4800

Now money lent on 5% = a = 4800

⇒ Money lent on 8% = 9300 - 4800 = 4500

Required ratio = 4800 : 4500

∴ Required Ratio = 16 : 15.
